rubric.result: The five sentences of `### Desired end state`, each measured against the sum of the ten commits. (1) `GET /sessions` answering `{"sessions":[{"id","name"}]}` with what the backend owns right now, each named by the program it runs: `sessions-route.ts` maps `listed.sessions` to `{id, name}` and nothing else, `PtyLiveSessions.all()` answers only what `#open` still holds, and `open()` names the session `#basenameOf(shell)` — the e2e asserts the literal body against the `LiveSession` the adapter really returned. (2) The SSE stream opening with the scrollback and carrying every later byte: `session-stream-route.ts` writes the three headers, subscribes, then writes one frame with `watched.printed`, and `PtyLiveSessions.#received` fans each chunk to every watcher; `P-2`'s `data: {"bytes":"…"}` and no `kind`. (3) `POST /sessions/:id/input` writing the text: `session-input-route.ts` → `TypeIntoSession` → `LiveSessions.write`, 202 `{"status":"typed","id"}`. (4) `ct-api.ts` opening one session at start-up and owning it, the close ending the stream and nothing else, a second subscription replaying the scrollback: `ct-api.ts:432-436` builds `PtyLiveSessions` with the real `node-pty` spawn and calls `liveSessions.open()` before the server exists; `request.on('close')` calls `watched.stop()` and `response.end()` and never reaches the port with anything else; `watch`'s `stop` deletes only that watcher; `session-channel-real-process.test.ts`'s second test cancels the reader, re-lists the session, types again and a SECOND subscription receives the echo. (5) The page rendering it in a real terminal emulator, listing the live ones and sending every keystroke: `SessionTerminal.tsx` builds `@xterm/xterm`'s `Terminal` at 80x24, opens it on its ref'd screen, writes every `bytes` into it and wires `terminal.onData((text) => void SessionsClient.type(session.id, text))`; `SessionsPanel.tsx` lists the names as `Button`s beside the chosen one's terminal; `Home.tsx` mounts the section unconditionally. Nothing a sentence promises is missing from the sum, and nothing an earlier commit produced was undone by a later one. Two things I checked because they are the sort a per-task judge cannot: all four methods of the `LiveSessions` port that Task 1 declared callerless now have a real production caller in the accumulated diff — `all()` from `ListLiveSessions.execute`, `find()` from both `SessionStreamRoute.handledBy` and `SessionInputRoute.handledBy`, `watch()` from `WatchLiveSession.execute`, `write()` from `TypeIntoSession.execute` — so the tension Task 1's judge let stand is resolved by the slice; and assumption 13 (the cabin's session is not reopened once its shell exits) breaks no sentence of the end state, which promises one session opened at start-up and never promises it perpetual — it is declared in §9, written into `backend/API.md`'s `GET /sessions` section and into `frontend/README.md`, and the page already renders both the empty list and the gone session, so it ships as a documented limit rather than as a gap.

Ten commits, read in order against each task's `**Objective:**`. The chain builds and never doubles back: T1 the port, the query and `GET /sessions`; T2 the adapter over an injected spawn; T3 the real `node-pty` at start-up; T4 the stream; T5 the input; T6-T8 the page's client, terminal and panel; T9 the wiring and the documents; T10 the end-to-end. Every intermediate state a task left is retired by a later task whose objective names the retirement: T4 and T5 mount their routes without collaborators, and T9's objective — 'the running backend reaches all three endpoints' — hands `liveSessions`, `WatchLiveSession` and `TypeIntoSession` to the `ApiServer` beside the `listLiveSessions` T3 wired, so no scaffolding for a half-wired backend survives. The two later commits that reach back into an earlier one's files are extensions, not reversals, and both are the amended plan's own words: T7 adds `onRefused` to T6's `SessionStreamListener` because a 400 before the SSE headers is not an unreachable backend, and T8 makes T7's terminal double record what `open(screen)` was given and pins it — T7's objective ('names what went wrong') and T8's own text ask for exactly those. The three `-` lines that touch an assertion (`Home.restoreWorkflow`, `Home.startPlan`) scope a query to its container because the panel adds a second live region to the page, which is the consequence of T8's 'in every stage' and weakens nothing. No two tasks solve the same problem two ways: one port, one adapter, one client, one `API_PATHS` entry that the dev server matches by prefix for all three endpoints. The eight protected endpoints are untouched across the whole sum — the only lines added to `api-server.ts` are the three new mount pairs and their collaborator fields, placed before `Failures.nothingMatched`. The change to `plugin/scripts/ct-step.mjs` in T10 is the one thing in the slice that is not the session channel, and it is not an incoherence: it is declared in the amended §4, §7 and `**Files:**`, it carries its own plugin test, it repairs a control that made the run's own state unsatisfiable rather than routing around it, and Task 10's judge already weighed it on its merits under `alcance` and did not report it — a decision that is settled before this judge and that I am not reopening.

The declared signal is 'the session list names the live session and its stream carries bytes while the process runs', measured against the accumulated diff and against `plugin/conventions/simplicity.md`. PRODUCTION CODE EMITS IT: both halves are produced by production lines, not by a test or a fixture — `sessions-route.ts` builds the named list from `ListLiveSessions`, `session-stream-route.ts` writes `data: {"bytes":…}` for the scrollback and for every chunk `PtyLiveSessions.#received` fans out, and beside them `pty-live-sessions.ts` emits two stderr lines, `live session ${session.id} (${program}) opened` and `… exited`, whose reader `simplicity.md` demands is named in the plan itself ('so whoever runs `make run-backend` can tell a live cabin terminal from a dead one'). THE REPO'S OWN INSTRUMENTATION: this backend instruments by taking a `stderr: (line: string) => void` sink through the constructor and letting `ct-api.ts` bind it to `process.stderr.write(line)` — the same shape the recovery diagnostic and the harvest clock already use; `PtyLiveSessions` takes exactly that collaborator and the wiring in `ct-api.ts:432-436` passes exactly that sink. No second logging library arrives with the slice: `node-pty` is the terminal and `@xterm/xterm` is the renderer, neither is an emit path. EVERY LABEL BOUNDED: the diff adds no metric and no dimension; the only unbounded value anywhere near an emit site is the session's `randomUUID` inside those two stderr lines and inside the `id` field of the answers, which is one line per session open and one per exit over the life of a backend that owns a handful of sessions — a log line's subject, not a label that multiplies series. The three checks hold; one smell is reported below as `low`, and it changes nothing about them.

findings.what: señal redundante: the cell restates this slice's first two acceptance criteria instead of naming something read in production. Both halves of the smell hold. First: what the signal promises — 'the session list names the live session and its stream carries bytes while the process runs' — is already verified by a test of this very diff, `session-channel-real-process.test.ts`'s `it('the live session is listed, its stream carries what it prints and what is typed reaches it')`, which lists the session over real HTTP, asserts the body against the `LiveSession` the adapter returned, and reads frames until the echoed token comes back through the stream; it comes true by running `npm --prefix backend test`, with nothing deployed. Second: what the cell names ends with that run — no metric, no log line and no event anyone reads in production after the merge. The slice does carry a real signal, `pty-live-sessions.ts`'s `live session <id> (<program>) opened/exited` on the injected stderr sink, with the reader the plan names (whoever runs `make run-backend`); the cell could have named that and did not. This is a defect of the cell as a declaration, written at groom time and already redundant before the first commit; the code is a separate matter and `estado-final` has already measured it.
